content.title: Foreground Fixation | Escalating Hazards and Task Reset
content.summary: Lock one adult and one small repeatable foreground task before background hazards escalate through clear proximity levels. Each event causes only the minimum avoidance, one near-contact peak creates the largest displacement, and the adult visibly resumes the same task afterward.

quick_start.input_format: clearly adult original protagonist and one small repeatable foreground task established first + at least three background hazards escalate through readable proximity levels + hands and gaze return to the same task after every hazard + minimal evasions precede one near-contact peak with the largest body displacement + adult resumes the original task after danger passes instead of celebrating or defeating the threat
quick_start.recommended_input: An adult greenhouse technician keeps calibrating an amber moisture meter while rear sprinklers burst, an empty cart crosses and one loose hose whips near the visor; after a sharp backward lean, the technician recovers and resumes the same calibration.
required_anchors: Establish one clearly adult original protagonist and one small repeatable foreground task before hazards escalate.
Escalate at least three hazards from background activity to near contact while keeping their direction legible.
Use the minimum avoidance needed until one near-contact peak causes the largest body displacement.
End with the adult resuming the task after danger passes, not celebrating or defeating the threat.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Lock one adult and one small repeatable foreground task before background hazards escalate through clear proximity levels. Each event causes only the minimum avoidance, one near-contact peak creates the largest displacement, and the adult visibly resumes the same task afterward.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Lock one original clearly adult protagonist and one small repeatable foreground task in a dangerous environment. Keep the task object visible and the hands or gaze continuously recoverable while background hazards escalate through at least three distinct proximity levels. Let each hazard force only the minimum physical adjustment required for survival, then return the adult to the identical task before the next escalation. Reserve the largest body displacement for one near-contact event without letting the task object disappear or change state. End after the hazard passes with the adult visibly resuming the same task, proving that fixation—not invulnerability—is the comic constant. The reusable mechanism is foreground task persistence, background-scale escalation, minimal avoidance, one near-contact peak and immediate behavioral reset—not the source man, face, armor, phone, battlefield, arrows, fire, exact camera, gestures, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Establish one clearly adult original protagonist and one small repeatable foreground task before hazards escalate.
invariants.purpose: Provides a stable behavioral baseline against which danger can be measured.
invariants.ablation_failure: Starting with chaos makes the fixation unreadable.

invariants.rule: Escalate at least three hazards from background activity to near contact while keeping their direction legible.
invariants.purpose: Builds a proximity ladder rather than random spectacle.
invariants.ablation_failure: Equal-intensity hazards create no comic progression.

invariants.rule: After each hazard, return hands and gaze to the same task object.
invariants.purpose: Makes fixation a repeated action instead of a one-time prop joke.
invariants.ablation_failure: Switching tasks breaks the behavioral pattern.

invariants.rule: Use the minimum avoidance needed until one near-contact peak causes the largest body displacement.
invariants.purpose: Preserves contrast while giving the escalation a climax.
invariants.ablation_failure: Large reactions too early flatten the ladder.

invariants.rule: End with the adult resuming the task after danger passes, not celebrating or defeating the threat.
invariants.purpose: Closes on behavioral persistence rather than heroics.
invariants.ablation_failure: A victory pose changes the mechanism into action competence.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source adult man, face, hair, earrings, blood marks and exact expressions
the source medieval armor, chain mail, red cloth, sword and smartphone
the source battlefield, fighters, fires, smoke, arrows, bodies and debris
the source exact two-thumb gestures, backward lean, arrow paths, orbit and framing
the source creator identity, Seedance 2.5 wording and 15-second timing
